_doc: Weekly Acceleration Watch — named startups showing the strongest GitHub engineering acceleration the week of `weekStart`. Each cohort is graded post-hoc against public fundraise / acquisition / shutdown news at the 60-day and 90-day windows. Methodology: ssrn.com/abstract=6606558.
_legal: This is a data-driven engineering activity watchlist generated from public GitHub data. It is not investment advice. Naming a company indicates that its observed engineering activity matches the patterns described in our methodology — it does not assert that the company is fundraising, will fundraise, or has any specific intent. Outcomes are recorded post-hoc from public announcements only.

_grading._doc: Outcome enum. `null` = not yet graded. Pending picks remain null until the 60d window closes.

values.raised: Public funding round announced (any stage) within the grading window.
values.acquired: Acquisition or merger announced within the grading window.
values.ipo: Public listing or direct listing announced within the grading window.
values.other_milestone: Other observable public milestone (major hire announced, product launch, named customer, partnership) but no funding event.
values.no_event: No publicly observable milestone within the grading window.
values.shutdown: Company shut down or paused operations.
values.excluded: Pick withdrawn from grading (data error, duplicate, or non-venture entity).

picks.name: zapplyjobs
picks.thesis: Pre-seed US jobs platform sustaining 1,694 commits over 14 days with the contributor signal pointing to a hiring burst. The combination of pre-seed stage and high commit volume is the textbook pre-seed-to-seed acceleration profile.

picks.name: atrocore
picks.thesis: EU seed-stage configurable PIM/MDM platform with a sustained framework-migration signal. The +38% acceleration on 116 commits indicates production-grade refactor work — usually a Series A precursor in B2B SaaS.

picks.name: ever-co
picks.thesis: Open-core ERP/HR platform showing a 9.5x acceleration over baseline with a contributor base of 79. A spike of this magnitude on a multi-product team usually maps to a release window or a customer-driven sprint.

picks.name: bakaphp
picks.thesis: LATAM seed-stage commerce engine with one of the highest commit volumes in the seed cohort. 598 commits / 14d with a +32% delta indicates real customer-driven shipping rather than open-source maintenance.

picks.name: JanssenProject
picks.thesis: Identity-and-access platform (Gluu spinout) with a +77% acceleration on a 100-contributor base. Framework migration in identity SaaS at this scale typically lines up with enterprise-tier launch or platform compliance work.

picks.name: metasfresh
picks.thesis: EU venture-backed open-core ERP with a 2.4x acceleration. Sustained framework migration plus 66 active contributors maps to a re-platform or a major customer onboarding.

picks.name: bagisto
picks.thesis: APAC open-core Laravel commerce platform with a +59% acceleration. Framework-migration commits with a 100-contributor base usually map to a major version release — a typical B2B fundraising-window precursor in the e-commerce stack.

picks.name: devcode-it
picks.thesis: Italian Series A/B devtools / SaaS shop with a +38% acceleration. Smaller velocity but high contributor:commit ratio (1:1) — a hallmark of distributed senior engineering teams shipping to production.

picks.name: third-culture-software
picks.thesis: Series A/B healthcare software shop with a +25% acceleration on a 28-person contributor base. Framework migration in regulated software (healthcare) is rare and meaningful — usually a product re-architecture financed by a recent or upcoming round.

picks.name: Lonero-Team
picks.thesis: Seed-stage decentralized infra team with a +28% acceleration. Smaller absolute volume but the framework-migration label across a 14-person contributor base indicates a real product re-platform rather than a single-author push.
